title: xtouch-daemon configuration
description: The configuration of xtouch-daemon (config.toml); `xtouch-daemon check-config` checks the rest.

aliases.description:
Names to show on `auto` strips for applications, at most 7 characters: for the name the sound server reports
(`xtouch-daemon list-apps`), the label, e.g. "Discord" for "WEBRTC VoiceEngine".
aliases.title: Aliases

mqtt.description: The MQTT broker, needed by `homeassistant` channels and controls.

voip.description: The participants of the voice chat, who share the `auto` slots: without the section, its defaults (`bridge`).

channel.description: The channels: what the strips control (devices, applications, people, Home Assistant).

tags.description: Words that group channels, for the conditions of slots (`present`) and the pools that take them.
tags.title: Tags

in_pool.description:
While no slot shows the channel, its pool hands it out: an `apps` channel like an application (`apps`, `auto`),
a `person` channel as one of the people (`people`, `auto`).
in_pool.title: In Pool

absent_after.description: Seconds the channel stays present after it had nothing to control any more; by default 3.
absent_after.title: Absent After

pool.description: The built-in pools (auto, apps, people, devices) and pools of your own.

auto.description:
`[pool.auto]`: the look of the strips of the applications on its slots. The people on them look as
`[pool.people]` says.

apps.description: `[pool.apps]`: the applications that play and have no slot, and the look of their strips.

from.description: The side the applications fill their slots from, in `apps` and in `auto`.
from.title: From

exclude.description: Applications that never get a slot of `apps` or `auto`.
exclude.title: Exclude

hold.description: Seconds a slot keeps an application after it stopped playing.
hold.title: Hold

people.description: `[pool.people]`: the people of the voice chat, their order and the look of their strips.

from.description: The side the people fill their slots from, in `people` and in `auto`.
from.title: From

order.description: The people by name or `person` channel, before the others. Those sit in the order they were first seen.
order.title: Order

devices.description: `[pool.devices]`: the outputs and inputs that no channel has, and the look of their strips.

from.description: The side the devices fill their slots from.
from.title: From

exclude.description: Devices that never get a slot of `devices`, by node name or description; `*` and `?` are wildcards.
exclude.title: Exclude

hold.description: Seconds a slot keeps a device after it went, e.g. while Bluetooth headphones reconnect.
hold.title: Hold

channels.description: The channels the pool hands out, by id or tag, in this order.
channels.title: Channels

from.description: The side the pool fills its slots from.
from.title: From

anyOf.description: `[pool.<id>]` with `kind = "apps"`: the applications of a group that play, one strip each.

kind.description: What the pool hands out: `apps`, the applications that match, or `people`, listed people of the voice chat.
kind.title: Kind

match.description: The applications it takes: parts of names or binaries, ignoring case, or presets like `@music`.
match.title: Match

exclude.description: Applications it never takes, though they match.
exclude.title: Exclude

from.description: The side the applications fill their slots from.
from.title: From

hold.description: Seconds a slot keeps an application after it stopped playing.
hold.title: Hold

anyOf.description: `[pool.<id>]` with `kind = "people"`: listed people of the voice chat, one strip each.

kind.description: What the pool hands out: `apps`, the applications that match, or `people`, listed people of the voice chat.
kind.title: Kind

people.description: Who it takes, by name as in the voice chat (ignoring case); this is their order.
people.title: People

from.description: The side the people fill their slots from.
from.title: From

state.description: The states and modes that the conditions of the slots ask about.

slots.description: The candidates of each slot (1 to 8, from the left): it shows the first whose condition holds.

anyOf.description: A channel or pool, maybe with a condition: `voip if call`.
A candidate as a table: what it shows, maybe a condition, and options of the place.

show.description: The channel or pool it shows, or - for nothing.

when.description: The condition, e.g. `call and not gaming`.

controls.description: Controls of a slot that act whatever it shows (1 to 8): one table, or a list of them.

BehaviorConfig.description: How the faders, encoders, meters and `auto` strips behave.

max_volume.description:
The volume, in percent, with a fader at the top. Above 100 % the audio is amplified. With 130, 100 % is at the 0
dB mark of the device and the fader is linear (see `unity_at`).
max_volume.title: Max Volume

unity_at.description:
Where 100 % is on the fader, in percent of its travel from the bottom; the device marks 0 dB at about 77. Above
the mark the fader goes on to `max_volume`. A strip whose range ends at 100 % stays linear.
unity_at.title: Unity At

encoder_step.description: Percent per step of an encoder: of the volume (`volume`), or of the number (`homeassistant`).
encoder_step.title: Encoder Step

reset_volume.description: The volume a push on a `volume` encoder sets, within the range of the strip.
reset_volume.title: Reset Volume

meters.description: The LED meters show the level. Off, every meter stays dark; `meter` turns off a single one.
meters.title: Meters

meter_point.description:
Where the meters take the level: before the volume and Mute of the strip, or after them. A channel or a place
may have its own `meter_point`.
meter_point.title: Meter Point

BehaviorConfig.title: BehaviorConfig

ButtonClaim.description: A button of `[controls]` as a table: what a press does, what its LED shows, or both.

press.description:
What a press does, whatever the slot shows: an action, an application to start, or a program to run. Unset: the
press stays with what the slot shows.

led.description:
What the LED shows, whatever the slot shows. A `watch` lights it with each line `on`, `1`, `true` or `yes`, and
flashes it on `flash`. Unset: what the press does.

ButtonClaim.title: ButtonClaim

ButtonConfig.description: What a button does: a press, a hold, and what its LED shows. Unset, each takes what the strip type does.

press.description: What a press does. An action that lasts while held (`talk`, `mute_others`) needs no `hold`.
press.title: Press

hold.description: What holding it for longer than half a second does; then a press acts when the button is let go.
hold.title: Hold

led.description: What its LED shows. A `watch` lights it with each line `on`, `1`, `true` or `yes`, and flashes it on `flash`.
led.title: Led

ButtonConfig.title: ButtonConfig

channel.description:
The `custom` channel whose value the fader or the encoder sets. A fader sets the value of its fader. An encoder
sets the value of its own encoder, else that of its fader. E.g. `screen_left`.
channel.title: Channel

ChoiceConfig.description: One of the devices a strip switches between with Select, maybe in a profile of its sound card.

label.description: The top line of the LCD while this choice is active; by default the start of the description of the device.
label.title: Label

device.description:
The device, by its node name or description (`xtouch-daemon list-devices`). `*` and `?` are wildcards, e.g.
`bluez_output.*` for the first Bluetooth headphones there are.
device.title: Device

card.description:
The sound card whose `profile` the choice needs, by its name (`alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4`) or description.
Wildcards work.
card.title: Card

profile.description:
The profile of `card` for this choice, by its name or description. Select switches the card to it first, then
makes the device the default.
profile.title: Profile

min_volume.description: The volume, in percent, with the fader at the bottom while this choice is active; by default that of the strip.
min_volume.title: Min Volume

max_volume.description:
The volume, in percent, with the fader at the top while this choice is active; by default that of the strip.
E.g. 200 for weak speakers.
max_volume.title: Max Volume

ChoiceConfig.title: ChoiceConfig

ControlsConfig.description:
Controls of a slot that act whatever it shows (`[controls]`), while `when` holds; of a list of them per slot the
first whose `when` holds.

fader.description:
What the fader of the slot sets, whatever the slot shows: a number in Home Assistant, the value of a `custom`
channel, or a value of your own.

encoder.description:
What the encoder of the slot sets, whatever the slot shows. The LED ring shows the value. E.g. `{ channel =
"screen" }`.

select.description:
What Select does, whatever the slot shows: an action, an application to start, or a program to run. As a table,
it takes a `press`, a `led` or both.

rec.description:
What Rec does, whatever the slot shows: an action, an application to start, or a program to run. As a table, it
takes a `press`, a `led` or both.

solo.description:
What Solo does, whatever the slot shows: an action, an application to start, or a program to run. As a table, it
takes a `press`, a `led` or both.

meter.description: What the meter of the slot shows, whatever the slot shows: Home Assistant's level, or a number a program prints.
meter.title: Meter

color.description:
The backlight of the LCD of the slot, whatever the slot shows: a color, Home Assistant's, or the color a program
prints.
color.title: Color

lcd.description:
The second line of the LCD of the slot, whatever the slot shows: Home Assistant's text, or the newest line a
program prints.
lcd.title: Lcd

when.description: The controls apply while this condition of states and modes holds, e.g. `not call`.
when.title: When

id.description: Names the Home Assistant entities of the slot's controls; by default `slot_<n>`.
id.title: Id

ControlsConfig.title: ControlsConfig

name.description: A part of the name of the sound card of the extender, as `/proc/asound/cards` lists it.
name.title: Name

virtual.description:
Drives the virtual device instead, to try things without the device (`xtouch-daemon virtual-device`, or the
GUI's). A reload switches to it, or back to the device.
virtual.title: Virtual

touch_required.description:
A fader changes its value only while you touch it, so a fader the motor moves changes nothing. Off, every move
counts, e.g. a fader pushed with a fingertip the sensor does not notice.
touch_required.title: Touch Required

touchless_faders.description:
Faders whose touch sensor is broken, numbered from 1 on the left. A move counts as a touch, half a second
without a move as letting go.
touchless_faders.title: Touchless Faders

startup.description: How the strips light up after the device connects.
startup.title: Startup

shutdown.description: How the strips go dark when the daemon stops.
shutdown.title: Shutdown

LaunchAction.description: A program a button starts, as in `[controls]`.

launch_when_running.description: Select starts `launch` also while the application runs, e.g. a `mumble://` URL that connects a running Mumble to a server.
launch_when_running.title: Launch When Running

LaunchAction.title: LaunchAction

LevelBinding.description: A meter that shows a number that a program of your own prints, between `min` and `max`.

watch.description:
A program that runs all the time and prints a number per change. The meter shows it. E.g. `["cpu-load",
"--watch"]`.
watch.title: Watch

min.description: The number with the meter dark.
min.title: Min

max.description: The number with the meter full.
max.title: Max

LevelBinding.title: LevelBinding

MqttConfig.description: The MQTT broker Home Assistant uses, for `homeassistant` strips.

host.description: The host name or address of the broker, e.g. "homeassistant.local" for the Mosquitto add-on.
host.title: Host

port.description: The port of the broker. 1883 is the usual one without TLS.
port.title: Port

username.description: The user to log in as. Without it, the daemon connects without logging in.
username.title: Username

password.description: The password. `password_file` or `password_env` keep it out of the configuration.
password.title: Password

password_file.description: A file with the password (`~` is your home directory). Whitespace around it is ignored.
password_file.title: Password File

password_env.description: An environment variable with the password, e.g. set with `systemctl --user edit xtouch-daemon` (`Environment=`).
password_env.title: Password Env

discovery_prefix.description: The MQTT discovery prefix of Home Assistant. Change it only if Home Assistant uses another one.
discovery_prefix.title: Discovery Prefix

namespace.description: The start of the entity IDs (`number.xtouch_strip_1_fader`) and the topics: lower case letters, digits and `_`.
namespace.title: Namespace

device_name.description: The name of the device in Home Assistant.
device_name.title: Device Name

MqttConfig.title: MqttConfig

ProfileConfig.description: A profile of the sound card of a device strip, e.g. analog or digital output.

label.description: The top line of the LCD while the card is in this profile, e.g. "Phones" for the analog output.
label.title: Label

profile.description:
The profile, by its name (`output:iec958-stereo+input:analog-stereo`) or description. `xtouch-daemon
list-devices` lists them.
profile.title: Profile

min_volume.description: The volume, in percent, with the fader at the bottom in this profile; by default that of the strip.
min_volume.title: Min Volume

max_volume.description:
The volume, in percent, with the fader at the top in this profile; by default that of the strip. E.g. 200 for
weak speakers.
max_volume.title: Max Volume

ProfileConfig.title: ProfileConfig

RunAction.description: A program of your own that a button runs to its end.

run.description:
The program a press runs, then each argument. `{value}` is the value of the fader, else of the encoder. E.g.
`["sysctrl", "display", "reset"]`.
run.title: Run

RunAction.title: RunAction

mode.description: It is a mode: one mode is on at a time, the one with the highest `priority` whose sources are on.
mode.title: Mode

label.description: What the LCDs show across the strips when the mode comes; by default its name.
label.title: Label

priority.description: Of several modes whose sources are on, the one with the highest priority is on.
priority.title: Priority

apps.description: On while one of these applications plays.
apps.title: Apps

recording.description: On while one of these applications records, e.g. with an open microphone.
recording.title: Recording

voice_chat.description: On while you are in a channel of the voice chat.
voice_chat.title: Voice Chat

processes.description: On while a process of one of these names runs.
processes.title: Processes

devices.description: On while one of these devices (outputs or inputs) is there.
devices.title: Devices

channels.description: On while one of these channels is present.
channels.title: Channels

homeassistant.description: On while its switch in Home Assistant is on. Needs `[mqtt]`.
homeassistant.title: Homeassistant

when.description: On while this condition of other states holds, e.g. `call and not gaming`. Instead of sources.
when.title: When

delay_on.description: Seconds its sources must be on before the state is.
delay_on.title: Delay On

delay_off.description: Seconds the state stays on after its sources went off; by default 3, for modes 10, for `when` 0.
delay_off.title: Delay Off

persist.description: An override lasts until you set it back, not only until the sources change.
persist.title: Persist

SwitchingConfig.description: The chord, and the banner of a new mode.

chord.description:
The strips whose Solo buttons, held together, do `chord_action`, numbered from 1 on the left; none for no chord.
Home Assistant still gets the presses of its strips.
chord.title: Chord

action.description:
What the chord does: `cycle_modes` (the next mode), `mode:<id>` or `toggle:<state or mode>`. In the file: `chord
= { strips = [1, 8], action = "toggle:call" }`.
action.title: Chord Action

banner.description:
Seconds the LCDs show the label of a new mode, and a slot that shows something else its new label and why. 0 for
none.
banner.title: Banner

chord_action.description:
What the chord does: `cycle_modes` (the next mode), `mode:<id>` or `toggle:<state or mode>`. In the file: `chord
= { strips = [1, 8], action = "toggle:call" }`.
chord_action.title: Chord Action

SwitchingConfig.title: SwitchingConfig

Target.description: One of the things a `custom` channel controls, e.g. one of two screens.

name.description: The name on the LCD while the strip controls it, e.g. `Left`.
name.title: Name

value.description: What `{target}` is in the programs of the channel, e.g. `DisplayPort-1`.
value.title: Value

Target.title: Target

ValueBinding.description: A value that programs of your own set and watch, e.g. the brightness of a screen.

set.description:
The program that sets the value, then each argument. `{value}` in an argument is the new value. E.g.
`["brightnessctl", "set", "{value}%"]`.
set.title: Set

watch.description:
A program that runs all the time and prints the value, one line per change. The fader, the LED ring and the LCD
follow it.
watch.title: Watch

min.description: The value with the fader at the bottom and the LED ring empty.
min.title: Min

max.description: The value with the fader at the top and the LED ring full.
max.title: Max

step.description: How much one step of the encoder changes the value. By default `behavior.encoder_step` percent of the range.
step.title: Step

push.description: The value a push of the encoder sets. Without it, a push does nothing. E.g. the full brightness.
push.title: Push

format.description: How the LCD shows the value, in the format of Python. E.g. `{value:.0%}` shows 0.55 as `55%`.
format.title: Format

ValueBinding.title: ValueBinding

VoipConfig.description: Where `voip` strips get the participants of the voice chat.

provider.description: Who tells the daemon the participants of the voice chat.
provider.title: Provider

participants.description: The names of the participants of the `demo` provider.
participants.title: Participants

VoipConfig.title: VoipConfig

WatchBinding.description: A part that shows what a program of your own prints: a line per change.

watch.description:
A program that runs all the time and prints a line per change. The part shows the newest line. E.g.
`["playerctl", "status", "--follow"]`.
watch.title: Watch

WatchBinding.title: WatchBinding

strip.choices.description:
The devices Select switches between, each maybe in a profile of its sound card. E.g. headphones on the analog
output, speakers on the digital one, Bluetooth headphones. Instead of `device` and `profiles`.

strip.color.description:
The backlight of the LCD. It goes dark while the strip has nothing to control, unless `lit_when_idle` is on. A
`watch` sets it with each line that is a color name.

strip.device.description:
The device, by its node name or description (`xtouch-daemon list-devices`); without it, the default device. With
several (a list, or wildcards like `bluez_output.*`), the strip shows the default one of them, and Select
switches between them.

strip.encoder.description: What the encoder does when you turn and push it. Its LED ring shows the value.

strip.fader.description: What the fader sets. Bound to something else, it gives the volume to the encoder.

strip.label.description:
The top line of the LCD; by default "Output", "Input" or the start of the description of the device. The label
of the active profile comes first.

strip.launch.description: A program that Select starts while none of the applications runs: the program, then each argument, e.g. `["mumble", "mumble://me@voice.example.org/Gaming"]`. It runs without a shell, so nothing is expanded.

strip.launch_when_running.description: Select starts `launch` also while the application runs, e.g. a `mumble://` URL that connects a running Mumble to a server.

strip.lcd.description:
The second line of the LCD, instead of the volume. A `watch` shows each line it prints. By default what the
strip type shows.

strip.lit_when_idle.description:
Keeps the LCD lit while the strip has nothing to control, e.g. no application plays or the device is not there.
The fader stays down.

strip.match.description:
The applications, by a part of their name or program (any case), e.g. "brave", or presets like `@browsers`,
`@voip`, `@games`. `xtouch-daemon list-apps` lists them.

strip.max_volume.description:
The volume, in percent, with the fader at the top; by default `behavior.max_volume`. Above 100 % the audio is
amplified, e.g. 200 for weak speakers.

strip.meter.description:
The LED meter shows the level. Needs `behavior.meters`. A `watch` makes it show each number it prints, from
`min` to `max`.

strip.meter_point.description:
Where the meter takes the level: before the volume and Mute of the strip, or after them. By default
`behavior.meter_point`.

strip.min_volume.description: The volume, in percent, with the fader at the bottom. E.g. 50 gives the whole fader to the upper half.

strip.mute.description: What Mute does (`press`, `hold`) and what its LED shows (`led`). By default nothing.

strip.person.description:
The participant the strip always shows: their name in the voice chat (any case), or several names of the same
person, e.g. "Alice" and "alice-phone". While they are away, the name shows dark.

strip.present.description:
A program that tells whether the channel is there: a line with text makes it present, an empty line absent.
Without it, the channel is always present.

strip.profiles.description:
Profiles of the sound card that Rec switches between, e.g. analog and digital output. Its LED is lit for every
profile but the first. `device` must match the device of every profile, e.g. `alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.*`.

strip.rec.description:
What Rec does (`press`, `hold`) and what its LED shows (`led`). By default it switches `profiles`; its LED shows
the profile, or else a recording. An indicator alone (`rec = "playing"`) sets the LED.

strip.select.description:
What Select does (`press`, `hold`) and what its LED shows (`led`). By default it makes the device the default
(with `device` or `choices`) or starts `launch`, and its LED shows that. `true`/`false` stand for that or nothing.

strip.solo.description:
What Solo does (`press`, `hold`) and what its LED shows (`led`). By default nothing. An indicator alone (`solo =
"muted"`) sets the LED.

strip.talking_color.description: The backlight of the LCD while the participant talks.

strip.targets.description:
The things the strip controls one at a time. `{target}` in the programs is the `value` of the target, the LCD
shows its `name`. Select's `next` switches. E.g. two screens.

strip.together.description: A move sets every target at once. The strip shows the first one.
